title: Ahab's Obsession
text:
The whaling ship Pequod sailed from Nantucket on what its owners and crew believed was an ordinary voyage for whale oil. Its captain, Ahab, stayed hidden in his cabin for days. When he finally appeared on deck, walking on a leg made of whale bone, he gathered the crew and nailed a gold doubloon to the mainmast. It would go to the first man to sight the white whale, Moby Dick, the whale that had taken his leg.

Ahab had the crew swear to hunt the white whale to the death, and in the excitement they cheered. Only the first mate, Starbuck, objected. He had come to hunt whales for profit, he said, not his captain's vengeance on a dumb animal, and to be enraged with a dumb thing seemed blasphemous. Ahab overrode him.

As the voyage went on, Ahab grew more consumed. He destroyed his navigation instrument. When the captain of another ship, the Rachel, begged for help searching for his lost son, Ahab refused. Starbuck once stood outside Ahab's cabin with a loaded musket, thinking of killing him to save the crew, and could not do it.

They found the whale. For three days Ahab chased it. On the third day the whale rammed and sank the Pequod, and Ahab, caught by his own harpoon line, was dragged under. Only the narrator, Ishmael, survived, floating on a coffin until the Rachel picked him up.
lesson: When a leader's personal goal quietly replaces the shared one, everyone pays for it. Watch for that in yourself, and do not let enthusiasm in the moment commit your people to someone else's obsession.
people: Captain Ahab, Starbuck, Ishmael, the crew of the Pequod
source: Herman Melville, Moby-Dick; or, The Whale, 1851
